Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalBank Holdings Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review GlobalBank Holdings's results for the Q2. With me this morning are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. GlobalBank Holdings delivered solid performance in the Q2, demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model and our commitment to serving our customers.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Enhancing customer experience
2. Driving operational efficiency
3. Investing in strategic growth initiatives
4. Maintaining strong capital levels.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on overall company performance. We achieved another standout quarter, with adjusted net revenues reaching $32.5 billion, up 11% year-over-year, fueled by sharp execution across our segments in a steady economic environment. Adjusted net income hit $8.1 billion, a 13% rise, delivering diluted EPS of $2.55—exceeding guidance and consensus by $0.25. Our return on tangible common equity climbed to 16.0%, from 14.5% last year, highlighting our sharp capital use and skill in handling sustained elevated rates.

Q2 net revenues advanced 14% quarter-over-quarter and 17% annually to $32.5 billion. Adjusted net income of $8.1 billion produced EPS of $2.55, topping Street forecasts. This reflects our broad platform: net interest income surged 21% year-to-date to roughly $20 billion, aided by our rate-sensitive assets and Fed hikes totaling over 500 basis points since 2022. Net interest margin widened 25 basis points to 3.50%, surpassing rivals like JPMorgan and Bank of America, due to smart deposit adjustments and a shift to higher-yield commercial lending.

Non-interest revenues, our key expander, increased 6% to $12.6 billion, powered by 19% growth in investment banking fees to $1.7 billion from M&A uptick in technology and healthcare—similar to major tech consolidations—and strong equity capital markets with IPO activity like recent tech listings. Wealth and asset management fees rose 8% to $4.6 billion, as assets under management reached $1.0 trillion, up 11%, with high-net-worth clients moving to fixed income near 4% Treasury yields. Payments and card volumes hit $300 billion, up 9%, supported by Visa and Mastercard collaborations in contactless tech.

Balance sheet expansion stayed measured: average loans grew 5% to $262 billion, with C&I up 8% on middle-market capital spending, consumer up 4%—mortgages steady amid high rates, autos and cards up 6% and 9%. Deposits expanded 7% to $355 billion, core low-cost at 67%, priced at 44 bps—better than industry norms via digital channels adding 600,000 new checking accounts. Loan-to-deposit ratio at 74%, with $71 billion in liquid assets.

Credit metrics stayed excellent: provisions at $1.0 billion, or 38 bps of loans, under our 45 bps cycle average. Net charge-offs rose to 51 bps from 41 bps, mainly cards with delinquencies at 2.7%, matching peers amid peak consumer debt. Non-accruals at 0.9%, criticized at 2.3%. CECL reserve at 1.24%, or $3.3 billion, ready for downturns.

By region, U.S. (64% revenues) grew 12%, consumer strong in Sun Belt and tech centers like Austin. Europe (21%) up 10% despite ECB paths, London IB at 14% ECM share. Asia-Pacific (11%) up 15% on ASEAN trade, wary on China under 2% loans. LatAm (4%) with 24% digital remittance growth via Alipay, Mercado Pago.

Tech-wise, Phase 2 core modernization on AWS cut costs 21%, real-time APIs for 80% of 3.8 million app users. AI fraud tool saved $110 million, up 29%; blockchain payments with Swift/Ripple handled $2.5 billion cheaper by 39%. Fintech embeds with Plaid/Stripe added $300 million fees.

We're leveraging trends: rate lift to NIMs, fee rebound, Basel clarity—CET1 at 13.8% beats proposed floors, supporting 14%+ payouts. Watch deposit betas to 54%, CRE office 1.1% loans (84% floating), geopolitics on 7% IB. Fortress metrics—LCR 124%, NSFR 117%—plus $3.8 billion buyback, 7% dividend boost show poise.

This sets us up for mid-teens ROTCE ahead.

Turning to capital ratios, our position fortifies our balance sheet for compliance, resilience, growth, and returns. CET1 at 13.8% fully loaded Basel III end-June, up 50 bps linked-quarter, 110 bps YoY. Tier 1 at 15.1%, aided by stable AT1 like our €300 million perpetual at 420 bps over swaps. Both exceed targets, with big buffers to regs.

Regulatory floors: Basel III/CRD IV/CRR sets CET1 min 7.8%—4.5% Pillar 1, 1.875% CCyB (pre-built for ECB moves), 1.5% G-SIB as Category 2, plus 2.5% conservation—for 10.3% total. Tier 1 11.8%. We have 350 bps CET1 excess, 330 bps Tier 1—strong in stress.

For CRR III/IV Basel final reforms from 2025, pro-forma CET1 12.8%, with real estate weights to 100% LGD, 72.5% output floor adding €4-5 billion RWAs. We're 250 bps ahead via derisking.

Drivers: 140 bps organic CET1 from earnings, reserves over €6 billion, offset by €125 million dividend at 42% payout. RWAs up 1% to €162 billion, tempered. IRB tweaks ECB-okayed for 5-10% relief on €10 billion mid-market, like BNP. Derivatives CVA/netting under EMIR cut 18 bps. Sold €750 million Nordic CRE legacy for €38 million gain to CET1.

Regions: North America €50 billion assets, CET1 14.1% post-CCAR, CECL ease, SBA/warehouse at 44% weights. Europe 13.0%, periphery sovereigns, pillar 2a 100 bps adds. UK WAM deleverages post-Brexit, PRA flat.

Levers: €500 million buyback 12 months, ECB-ok, 2% cap. M&A room €2.5 billion, APAC fintechs vs Nubank. Green AT1 Q3 for €1.25 billion transition, RWA relief pilots.

This strength shows prudent management amid U.S. regionals, Euro outflows—optimized for growth.

On risk-weighted assets management, a core to capital optimization under Basel III/IV, U.S. Endgame, EU CRR3. CET1 13.8% fully loaded tops 12-13% target, 10.5% min with buffers.

Q2 total RWA $295 billion, down 2% QoQ, 3.8% YoY, despite 6% loans in IB/WM. Density 41%, from 44% YoY, low-risk growth focus.

Breakdown: credit 82% $242 billion, -3% QoQ via management. Market $21 billion 7%, SA-MR VaR hedging pre-FRTB. CCR $11 billion SA-CCR up slight seasonal derivs, collateral cut add-ons 11%. Op risk $20 billion SMA +1% volumes, AMA review.

Compression drivers: $3.75 billion EMEA NPL sales Italy/Spain RE at 91% recovery, weights 150% to zero, like UniCredit/Santander ECB normalize. Securitization: $3 billion U.S. RMBS AAA <7% weights vs 35-50% on-books, Q3 pipeline $5 billion.

Models: IRB 92% credit, recalibrated PD/LGD corporate using ML-enhanced data for efficiency.

These moves optimize capital for returns.

Finally, cost of deposits, key to NIM in high-rate persistence. Average deposit cost 2.75%, +65 bps YoY, +20 bps QoQ, re-pricing $38 billion franchise, -1% QoQ seasonal commercial.

By mix: non-interest DDA 28% beta 0.05% steady. Interest-bearing 72% 3.20%—checking 1.85%, savings 3.45%, time 4.10%. Beta ~45% since Mar 2022 Fed cycle, below KeyCorp/Fifth Third 55-60%, sticky transactional.

Competition up: fintechs Ally 4.20%, SoFi/Marcus 4.30-4.50% drawing wholesale. MM/brokered compressed 14 bps. Consumer: Treasury Prime sweeps up retail savings +25 bps May.

Regional: Southeast (Florida/TX 35%) 2.50%, relationship DDA SMB. West Coast CA 22% 3.15%, credit unions SVB promo CDs 4.75%. Northeast 18% avg, HNW outflows JPM Private.

Counters: dynamic pricing engine Bloomberg/LDR tiers—MM cap 3.75% <$250k, loyalty 4.25% >$1M combined. Core +3% YoY.

Digital: FlexEarn Checking yields 2.50% wealth hooks, 37,500 accts $625M inflows 28 bps below savings. Commercial: treasury sweeps Geldwire auto.

Strategy: cut 5-7% time deposits/brokered 4.50% runoff Q3. NIM 3.45% +11 bps, costs 2.85-2.95% Q3 post-Sep 25 bps cut CME. $12.5M AI propensity non-interest to 32% 2025 like PNC/USB.

Disciplined betas/regional/tech sustain low-cost.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, John, and good morning. GlobalBank Holdings reported net income of $2.1 billion for the Q2, or $1.65 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 10% driven by higher interest rates and loan growth. Non-interest income saw moderate growth in fees offset by softer trading. We continue to maintain a strong capital position with a CET1 ratio of 13.8%. We are pleased with the progress we are making on our strategic initiatives, and we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable value for our shareholders.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, that is 1 then the star key. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide some color on deposit cost trends and competitive pressures?

John Reynolds:
Good morning, John. As John outlined earlier, our deposit costs rose to 2.75% amid re-pricing, but our beta at 45% lags peers due to sticky core deposits. We've used dynamic pricing and products like FlexEarn to manage competition from Ally and SoFi, growing core while targeting mix shifts. This supports NIM expansion, with moderation expected as rates ease.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. What is your outlook for RWA and capital deployment in the coming quarters?

Michael Chen:
Good morning, Emily. We're focused on continued RWA discipline, targeting further compression through sales, securitizations, and model tweaks, keeping density low. With CET1 at 13.8% and surplus buffers, we have capacity for buybacks up to $500 million and selective M&A, all while staying ahead of Basel reforms. Expect steady optimization supporting returns.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of commercial real estate on your loan portfolio?

Lisa Patel:
Good morning, David. CRE remains a small piece at about 8% of loans, with office at 1.1% mostly floating-rate and repriced. We've derisked via sales like our recent legacy disposals, keeping non-accruals low at 0.9%. Provisions reflect cycle prudence, and our CECL covers potential softening, but overall credit quality is solid with close monitoring.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to John Reynolds for any closing remarks.

John Reynolds:
Thank you for your interest in GlobalBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
